A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original Gaussian-composition simulations and Stable Diffusion alignment and composition experiments, including numerical results and generated images.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional AudioLDM concept-composition and combined reward/KL-constraint results in Appendices G.5 and G.7.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 and the surrogate-score composition procedure are retained. Appendix G.7 adds a limited combined-training variant enforcing KL constraints against two reference models together with a saturation-reward constraint; v1 discussed combining formulations without implementing this specific variant.

E1.justification: V2 extends evaluation beyond synthetic distributions and image generation to text-to-audio concept composition using AudioLDM. It also evaluates simultaneous reward alignment and composition constraints, a task combination previously left for further investigation.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in retained experiments are unchanged. Audio composition extends the existing Combined Prompting and Equal Weights comparisons to another modality. Appendix G.1 discusses other approaches but does not report evaluating them as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The added audio experiment introduces minimum CLAP scoring, while the combined-constraint experiment evaluates initial/final feasibility against two KL constraints and a reward constraint. Retained image metrics, 50-pair/50-triplet evaluations and corresponding retained settings tables are unchanged. Missing concept-composition hyperparameters do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: V2 adds training-overhead comparisons in Appendix G.8 and expands qualitative cases, including lemon/dandelion composition and additional animal examples. The existing constraint-threshold sensitivity analysis is relocated into G.6 with unchanged results.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 7 and v2 Figure 6 report the same standard-deviation bars across eight prompts with four samples each. Reward normalization statistics are also retained. The new checklist introduces no additional seed information, repeated-run procedure, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New audio results report minimum CLAP scores of 0.816, 1.57 and 1.92 for Combined Prompting, Equal Weights and Constrained, respectively (v2 Table 6). Table 12 adds combined-constraint outcomes, including final KL values of 0.101 and 0.097. Runtime measurements and additional generated examples are also new. Retained image benchmark scores and threshold-sensitivity values are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly conditions Theorems 2/4 on representability of every path distribution, previously invoked in their proofs, and removes the unequal-schedule KL and guidance-ratio derivations. Central mathematical expressions also change: Equation (3) drops the squared drift coefficient retained in Appendix C.1, and Lemma 7 replaces the continuous/discrete divergence comparison with identical terms. These changes affect mathematical substance beyond proof relocation or notation.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain unified constrained alignment/composition, characterization of optimal distributions and dual-based algorithms. V2 highlights the already-existing point-wise KL result in its introduction. Comparative advantages over equal weighting remain claimed there, despite their omission from the revised abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 explains why unavailable intermediate scores prevent applying its point-wise KL approach to alignment, interprets the audio results as improved concept balance, and discusses computational overhead. It removes v1's guidance-ratio explanation of balanced concept guidance. Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G.8 adds A6000 hardware, runtime and dual-update convergence information. Conversely, v1 Table 4's concept-composition settings—including batch size, epochs, DDIM steps, dual learning rate and guidance ratio 0.02—are absent from v2. The implementation repository link is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for CLAP and AudioLDM. New Appendix G.1 explains why superposition, projected sampling and specialized fixed-loss constraint methods are not directly applicable baselines. The existing related-work discussion and broader positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The introduction is reorganized into formulation, theory and empirical contributions, and substantial prose is rewritten throughout the main text. New subsection hierarchies separate distribution-space and diffusion-model treatments, while detailed supporting proofs move into a separate appendix. V2 also adds the conference checklist and revises author affiliations.

P2.justification: V2 adopts conference formatting and substantially resizes and rearranges displays, including placing Figure 5 beside Table 1. V1 Figure 6 becomes an expanded appendix Table 5. New audio and combined-constraint tables appear, the concept-hyperparameter table disappears, and the final image grids expand and change order.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens empirical support through audio and combined-constraint experiments, improves organization and discloses computational costs. However, it removes useful concept-composition settings and introduces inconsistencies in central KL mathematics: Equation (3) conflicts with its proof, and Lemma 7 loses its meaningful continuous/discrete comparison. These empirical and expository gains coexist with losses in mathematical consistency and reproducibility, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
